source: The Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Apophthegmata Patrum). Public-domain English translations (Wallis Budge, Helen Waddell). Used as a fallback on Today when the headline saint has no entry in the registry's quotes array. Rotated by day-of-year so the same line does not appear two days running.

sayings.text: I saw the snares of the enemy spread out over the world, and I groaned and said, What can pass through these? And I heard a voice saying, Humility.
Our life and our death is with our neighbour. If we win our brother, we win God; if we cause our brother to stumble, we have sinned against Christ.
Whoever has not been tried by temptation cannot enter the Kingdom of Heaven; take away temptations, and no one would be saved.
He who sits in solitude and is quiet hath escaped from three wars: hearing, speaking, seeing; but against one thing shall he continually battle: that is, his own heart.
If a man does not say in his heart, in the world there is only myself and God, he will not gain peace.
Go, sit in thy cell, and thy cell shall teach thee all things.
If you cannot keep silence, speak as if you were before God; for you are before Him.
Do not give your heart to that which does not satisfy your heart.
Pray as you can, not as you cannot.
If a man's deeds are not in harmony with his prayer, he labors in vain.

A brother said to Abba Sisoes: I see myself always in the presence of God. The old man said to him: It is not very great that thy thought should be with God; but it is great when a man sees himself lower than every creature.
Forgive, and you shall be forgiven; this fulfils the law.
